review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for proof blocks repeated across declarations and compared the candidates. I checked the definitions of transposeInvN, unipotentGL2 and UnramifiedWhittaker.unipotent. I also grepped other P2M/Sol files to see how the lemmas are reused. The only case that cleared the bar of nontrivial repeated reasoning is the pair weyl2_mul_transposeInvN_unipotent / weyl2_mul_transposeInvN_unipotentGL2. I considered and rejected the following, as short or only loosely similar: transposeInv3_map vs transposeInvN_map (different definitions), localAt_unipotentGL2 vs glArch_unipotentGL2 (short fin_cases proofs), and the 4-line unipotent-membership-to-phase extraction in norm_R_unipotent_mul vs solution (different shape). I have not compiled the proposed rewrite. The proposal assumes the stated defeq `unipotent x = unipotentGL2 x` (proved by Units.ext rfl at line 147) can be used with rw.

findings.problem: Both lemmas prove the same statement. For the Weyl element w₀ = [[0,1],[1,0]], w₀ * transposeInvN (unipotent x) = unipotent (-x) * w₀. One is stated for fields and UnramifiedWhittaker.unipotent, the other for commutative rings and unipotentGL2. Both proofs run the same four steps. They prove the inverse of the unipotent (once by Matrix.inv_eq_left_inv with simp, once via unipotentGL2_add), then unfold to matrices, rewrite with hinv and hw₀, and finish with `ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp`. The file already proves `unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2 : unipotent x = unipotentGL2 x := Units.ext rfl` (line 147), but only after the first lemma and without using it. The field version is therefore a special case of the ring version. The matrix computation and the inverse computation are maintained twice.
findings.proposed_change: Move `unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2` (line 147) above line 119. Delete the first proof and make it a corollary of the general lemma: `theorem weyl2_mul_transposeInvN_unipotent {F} [Field F] (w₀ : GL (Fin 2) F) (hw₀ : ...) (x : F) : w₀ * transposeInvN (Fin 2) (unipotent x) = unipotent (-x) * w₀ := by rw [unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2, unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2]; exact weyl2_mul_transposeInvN_unipotentGL2 w₀ hw₀ x`. The remaining ring-level proof is the only place that does the 2×2 entrywise computation. Optionally, extract the shared inverse fact `(unipotentGL2 x)⁻¹ = unipotentGL2 (-x)` as a named lemma proved by `inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_right (by rw [← unipotentGL2_add, add_neg_cancel, unipotentGL2_zero])`. The 3×3 lemma `longWeyl3_mul_transposeInv3_iotaGL_unipotent` (line 106) has its own `hinv` block that repeats the same inverse computation and could use that lemma for `unipotent`.
findings.benefit: This removes about 14 lines of duplicated matrix and inverse reasoning. Any change to the Weyl/unipotent computation is then made in one place. The relationship between the two `unipotent` notions becomes explicit instead of being two independently proved copies. The file also contains no wrapper or branch-moving trick: the corollary is a two-line rewrite.
